name: trilattice SIXTEEN_3

phase_0.boundary_condition: the set of all 16 elements of the trilattice SIXTEEN_3, closed under the three lattice orders

VINIT.justification: the initial uninitialized state before any element is distinguished

TANCH.justification: the maximal element that contains all others, bounding the system

AFWD.justification: moving from a lesser to a greater element along the trilattice order

AREV.justification: moving from a greater to a lesser element, the inverse of AFWD

CLINK.chosen_element: sequential composition of meet and join
CLINK.justification: chaining lattice operations to form complex transformations

IMSCRIB.justification: every element is itself; self-recognition in the lattice

FSPLIT.chosen_element: decomposition into truth and falsity components
FSPLIT.justification: splits an element x into its truth component t and falsity component f, such that x = t ⊕ f in the bilattice sense

FFUSE.chosen_element: recomposition from truth and falsity components
FFUSE.justification: recombines t and f into the original x via the lattice operation ⊕, verifying FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x

EVALT.justification: the affirmative part of an element, representing truth valuation

EVALF.justification: the negative part, representing falsity valuation

ENGAGR.chosen_element: paradical element with maximal truth and maximal falsity
ENGAGR.justification: an element that is both fully true and fully false, held without resolution

IFIX.chosen_element: fixed point of a monotone operator
IFIX.justification: a permanent record of a lattice element that remains unchanged under a given transformation

phase_3.void_description: bottom element ⊥: no information, uninitialized state (00)
phase_3.true_description: element with maximal truth and minimal falsity, representing pure affirmation (01)
phase_3.false_description: element with minimal truth and maximal falsity, representing pure negation (10)
phase_3.both_description: paradical element with maximal truth and maximal falsity, simultaneously holding both (11)

steps.domain_action: from the bottom element ⊥, begin the composition
move upward to a generic element x along the order
decompose x into its truth component t and falsity component f
affirm the truth component t as the positive branch
deny the falsity component f as the negative branch
recombine t and f to recover the original element x
identify the result with itself, confirming identity
move from x upward to a greater element y
compose the decomposition and recomposition steps as a single transformation
evaluate the paradical element where t and f are both maximal
return from the paradical element to a consistent element
reach the top element ⊤, the boundary
record the top element as a fixed point, irreversible

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the function mapping logical formulas to lattice elements and operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: communication via the partial order: elements exchange information through meet and join
phase_5.memory_mechanism: storage of lattice elements as nodes in the trilattice structure
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: bottom-up evaluation from ⊥ to ⊤, with lazy recomputation of components
phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical enumeration of all 16 elements with their truth and falsity components

phase_6.post_cycle_state: the result element after meet or join
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — lattice operations are homomorphic and preserve the structure of the trilattice
